subject: Cognitive Science
title: The Wisdom of Crowds
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Wisdom of Crowds.

hook.text: In 1906, a crowd guessed an ox's weight. The average was off by just one pound. No individual was that close.

buildup.text: James Surowiecki showed that diverse, independent groups often outperform individual experts.

discovery.text: Aggregation cancels individual errors. Each person's bias goes in a different direction, leaving the truth.

twist.text: It only works when judgments are independent. Let people see each other's answers and herding kills it.

climax.text: Prediction markets, Wikipedia, and jury systems all tap crowd wisdom—when structured to avoid groupthink.

punchline.text: Many independent minds beat one brilliant one.

quiz.question: What condition is required for crowd wisdom to work?
options: Judgments must be independent of each other
